now.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
now.text: May finds Norman Osborn lost and frightened at F.E.A.S.T. and helps him, believing he can be cured. When the Goblin takes control again he beats her and fatally wounds her.
now.on_a_card_about_b: A lost man May helps at F.E.A.S.T. His Goblin side kills her.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The kind woman who helps Norman, until the Goblin kills her.

proposed.text: May finds Norman Osborn lost and frightened at F.E.A.S.T. and helps him, believing he can be cured. When the Goblin takes control again, his glider strikes her down and fatally wounds her.

changes.evidence: Spider-Man: No Way Home: in the condo lobby May injects the Goblin with the antidote; the Goblin Glider then stabs her in the side and his pumpkin bombs go off. He does not beat her.

now.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
now.text: With Sandman's help, Peter cuts Max Dillon off from his power and brings him to the Sanctum to be cured. Max rips the cure off, steals an Arc Reactor and turns on him, until Otto helps the Spider-Men cure him.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Electro from another world. Steals an Arc Reactor before Peter cures him.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A young Spider-Man who tries to cure Max and finally does.

proposed.text: With Sandman's help, Peter cuts Max Dillon off from the power lines and sends him to a cell in the Sanctum. Later Max rips the cure off, steals an Arc Reactor and turns on him, until Otto helps the Spider-Men cure him.

changes.evidence: Spider-Man: No Way Home: after the power-line fight Peter teleports Electro to a Sanctum cell so Strange can send him home; Peter only decides to cure the visitors later, after Strange explains their fates.

now.title: The Defenders#2
now.text: Alexandra needs the Iron Fist to open a mystical door beneath Midland Circle, and she hunts Danny Rand for it.
now.on_a_card_about_b: The man Alexandra hunts, needing the Iron Fist to open K'un-Lun's door.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The Hand's leader, who hunts Danny for the Iron Fist.

proposed.title: The Defenders#3
proposed.text: Alexandra demands the Iron Fist's location from Stick. When Danny confronts the Hand at Midland Circle, she mocks him about K'un-Lun and sends her soldiers and Elektra after him, wanting him taken alive.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: The Iron Fist, whom Alexandra wants taken alive.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: The Hand's leader, who hunts Danny for the Iron Fist.

split.title: The Defenders#6
split.text: Elektra brings the captured Danny to Alexandra, who tells him the Hand only wants to return to K'un-Lun and that he will serve her like so many before him.
split.on_a_card_about_b: The Iron Fist, captured and brought before Alexandra.
split.on_b_card_about_a: The Hand's leader, who tells the captured Danny he will serve her.

changes.evidence: In The Defenders #2 (Mean Right Hook) Alexandra only learns of the blocked wall and has Stick captured; she first asks for the Iron Fist in #3 (Worst Behavior) and meets Danny at Midland Circle there. That the Hand needs the Iron Fist to open the door is only learned in #5-#6 (Sowande's words; Stick plans to kill Danny so the Hand cannot use him to open their locked door). In #6 Elektra brings Danny to Alexandra.

now.title: The Defenders#6
now.text: Bakuto and Sowande are two of the five founders of the Hand. After Davos kills Bakuto, Sowande helps bring him back, and Bakuto is horrified when Sowande later dies.
now.on_a_card_about_b: A fellow Hand founder, who helps bring Bakuto back to life.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A fellow Hand founder Sowande helps bring back to life.

proposed.text: Bakuto and Sowande are two of the five founders of the Hand. When the Hand's leaders learn that Stick has killed Sowande, Bakuto is horrified.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A fellow Hand founder, whose death horrifies Bakuto.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A fellow Hand founder, horrified by Sowande's death.

changes.evidence: The Defenders #6 (Ashes, Ashes): Stick sends Sowande's head to the Hand and Murakami, Bakuto and Gao are angered and horrified. Nothing on screen shows Sowande helping bring Bakuto back after Davos killed him (Iron Fist S1); Bakuto's body was just taken by the Hand, and the two never share a scene.

now.title: The Defenders#5
now.text: After Luke captures Sowande, the Defenders interrogate him, and he mocks Danny as the dumbest Iron Fist he has ever met. When he tries to escape, he holds a knife to Danny's throat and reveals that the Hand needs the Iron Fist, before Stick kills him.
now.on_a_card_about_b: A Hand captive who mocks Danny and holds a knife to his throat.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The Iron Fist the Hand needs, whom Sowande mocks and holds at knifepoint.

proposed.text: After Luke captures Sowande, the Defenders interrogate him, and he mocks Danny as the dumbest Iron Fist he has ever met. When he tries to escape, he holds a shard of glass to Danny's throat and reveals that the Hand needs the Iron Fist, before Stick kills him.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A Hand captive who mocks Danny and holds glass to his throat.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: The Iron Fist the Hand needs, whom Sowande mocks and holds hostage.

changes.evidence: The Defenders #5 (Take Shelter): Sowande frees himself, strikes Danny in a pressure point and holds a glass shard to his throat before Stick beheads him. He has no knife.

now.title: Luke Cage S2#3
now.text: Misty and Colleen team up as partners in fighting crime.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Colleen's close friend and crime-fighting partner.
now.on_b_card_about_a: Misty's close friend and crime-fighting partner.

proposed.text: Colleen helps Misty learn to box with one arm, and when men at a bar pick a fight, the two of them beat them all.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Colleen's close friend, who learns to fight one-armed with her.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Misty's close friend, who helps her learn to fight with one arm.

changes.evidence: Luke Cage S2#3 (Wig Out): Misty practices fighting with one arm with Colleen and lets out her frustration; at a bar they get into a fight and beat the men. They do not team up as crime-fighting partners there.

now.title: Iron Fist S2#9
now.text: Misty fights beside Danny and Colleen Wing against Davos.
now.on_a_card_about_b: A friend who fights beside Danny against Davos.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A friend Misty fights beside against Davos.

proposed.text: Misty returns with a police task force to capture Davos. She and the police reach the community center as Danny and Colleen fight off Davos's gang.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A friend who brings a police task force to help Danny stop Davos.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A friend Misty brings a police task force to help against Davos.

split.title: Iron Fist S2#10
split.text: Misty escapes Walker's captivity and helps Danny stop Walker by triggering Mary.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A friend who helps Danny stop Walker.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A friend who helps Misty stop Walker.

changes.evidence: Iron Fist S2#9 (War Without End): Misty returns with a task force and arrives at the community center after Colleen fights the gang off; she does not fight Davos, and Walker then attacks her. In S2#10 (A Duel of Iron) she wakes, escapes and helps Danny stop Walker by triggering Mary while Colleen fights Davos.

owner_calls.question: Cleary's only scene with Happy (questioning him about missing Stark tech, with Matt beside him) is in the extended 'More Fun Stuff Version' of No Way Home, not the theatrical cut. Does that count as the screen?
options: Keep the pair as is (extended cut counts)
owner_calls.evidence: The fandom P. Cleary and Matt Murdock pages cite only SMNWHTMFSV (The More Fun Stuff Version) for the Cleary and Happy interrogation. In the theatrical cut Matt only warns Happy he is under investigation.

owner_calls.question: The Avengers never names Thanos: the Other's master is only seen in the mid-credits scene, and the name is first said in Guardians of the Galaxy. The Avengers stages of loki|thanos, loki|the-other and thanos|the-other say 'Thanos' in their text and card lines. Should those lines say 'the Other's master' instead, or is the name OK because the person node is called Thanos anyway?
options: Reword them to 'the Other's master' / 'his master'
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia's The Avengers article says Whedon included Thanos in the post-credits scene 'even though the character is not identified in the film'; Feige confirmed the master is Thanos in an interview.
